correctness.rationale: The right kernel of a Gaussian (m−1)×m matrix is an unoriented uniform line. Its independent Gaussian signs give event probability 2^(1-m) and the positive normalized null vector gives the exact half-normal weight law under deterministic column scaling. The barycentric density follows from a rigorous positive radial Jacobian and gamma integration. Under single-column scale tau_m, an exact quotient X0/(X0+tau_m S_m) yields all three regimes by the strong law; the critical density and erfc threshold follow by explicit transformation; the Gaussian-mixture fluctuation follows by independent CLT and delta method; and the ordinary-vertex empirical and squared-weight limits by the strong law. A standalone Cartesian Gaussian-matrix checker and quadrature support finite formulas. Strict positivity of scales and nondegeneracy are explicitly required; finite simulations do not replace limiting proofs.

value.rationale: The conditional barycentric representation is a natural exact geometric observable for a rare Gaussian simplex that absorbs the origin; unlike the old event probability it detects anisotropic column scales. The entire family of weights exhibits a dimension-dependent singular allocation threshold tau_m≈1/m, an explicit nondegenerate critical law and fluctuation, and a diffuse ordinary-vertex profile, with a sharp distinction between holding an event and allocating its positive coordinates. This exact high-dimensional shape law has plausible uses in random convex feasibility and anisotropic geometric sampling; it is neither an arbitrary finite slice nor a mere restatement of a known Gaussian simplex volume.
